assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Restoring the dense equality matrix and clearing SPARSE_INDEXED_BUILD makes contour_tree.SPARSE_INDEXED_BUILD False, so this assertion reddens; sparse-build/negative_control.log shows exactly that with EXIT=1 and test_sparse_indexed_build_marker_is_present in the summary.

The digest is compared against _BASE_INTEGER_DIGESTS, constants recorded from the base build's own receipts, so it reddens whenever the head build's six integer/boolean arrays diverge from the base build's; it is independent of the head code because the right-hand side was not produced by it.

The expected side is vertex_flux[node_vertex], built from the array the test itself passed in, so it holds trivially if the build both mis-gathers and reports the same wrong node_vertex; its independence rests on node_vertex being pinned by the digest at line 113.

findings.text: follow-on: the node goal's outcome is not delivered - the four-rung exponent is unchanged at about 1.50 (sparse-build/h200/comparison.json) and the 10,000-cell whole read is 72.0-75.9 s against the 10 s target; the remaining dominant cost is the unchanged _sweep_tree fori_loop, named but not instrumented, so near-linear scaling is work for a next node rather than a defect to repair here.

follow-on: the after arm is an assembly, not one process at the head - six of its seven files are carried forward from 94d532f63 (job 1290984) and only the sparse-build file ran at bbc9f37a, justified only because 94d532f63..bbc9f37a touches no file but the test and the fragment.
